chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ammar al-Sabaty, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Every Muslim, between two Muslims, who reneges from Islam and denies the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) of his prophethood and belies him, then his blood is permissible for whoever hears that from him, and his wife is irrevocably divorced from him on the day he reneges, and his wealth is distributed among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of the one whose husband has died, and it is upon the Imam to kill him if they bring him to him, and he does not ask him to repent.'
ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences for a Muslim who denies the prophethood of the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific legal consequences of major apostasy (riddah) by denying Prophet Muhammad's prophethood, establishing that the apostate's blood becomes permissible to spill and his wife is immediately divorced. Notably, it specifies that the Imam executes the apostate without first inviting him to repent (istitab), a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence. The ruling also clarifies that wealth is distributed to heirs and the wife observes the waiting period of a deceased spouse, emphasizing the finality of the apostasy.
